Energy storage 📈 Job opportunities 📈 Antora Energy ’s Project Big Stone energy storage system is helping meet rising energy demands and creating workforce opportunities in the process! This project went from empty lot to energy production in less than a year and has supported more than 300 jobs—from industrial California to rural South Dakota. Check out this featured project from one of our #GCxN alum: https://lnkd.in/gfxMrJPk

Today, we're proud to announce that Antora has closed $550 million in Series C funding, co-led by G2 Venture Partners and Eclipse , to meet surging energy demand across industry, data centers, and the grid. From the beginning, we’ve always believed that the best way to advance our mission is to go big and go fast. With this funding, Antora will expand production and accelerate the deployment of large-scale projects across the country and around the world. “From factories to data centers, energy is the bottleneck to industrial growth,” said Andrew Ponec, Co-Founder and CEO of Antora. “Antora has shown we can help break that bottleneck—delivering energy fast, at massive scale, with American innovation.” Read more in Bloomberg: https://lnkd.in/gUe2tjmC

As I reflect on my time in NYC this past quarter, I’ve realized how intense, but incredibly rewarding it truly was. Through the Stanford in New York program, I had the wonderful opportunity to intern at the Permanent Mission of the UAE to the UN - New York , while balancing evening classes across the city. I wrapped up the quarter with the McKinsey & Company Edad Program, where I developed practical consulting skills through hands-on case work, and also joined the Stanford WIB NYC Trek gaining insights from firms like JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley. Feeling extremely grateful for the people I met, the spaces I got to be in, and everything I learned along the way.

In June 2025, Sultan Al Juhani , a KGSP sophomore majoring in Nuclear Engineering at University of California, Berkeley , took a break from his summer enrichment internship through the University of Illinois' FoDOMMaT research lab at the National Center for Supercomputing Applications to travel to Seoul, South Korea, to participate in the AFI Global Pitch Challenge at the ODC Organoid Developer Conference. Along with his teammates, Mohammed Bukhari , Noor Masri , Giovanna Lima , and Luana Lima , Sultan represented UC-Berkeley and the KGSP in this international competition putting forward innovative ideas for attaining more ethical treatment of animals while advancing scientific discovery. Sultan and his teammates presented their own vision to reduce animal testing in science through a machine learning model called SkipLab, for which a panel of judges awarded them first place and a monetary prize of $7000. He returned to Illinois with more confidence and excitement about "connecting artificial intelligence with real-world challenges." Read more about Sultan's experiences with machine learning and supercomputing this summer here: https://lnkd.in/eJNFPCUr

I'm excited to share that I've been given the opportunity to explore internship opportunities at NVIDIA. I want to thank Bridget Nahale for reaching out to me from Caroline Vesling's email account with this exciting opportunity. I'm not sure why their email contained incorrect punctuation at times, but they were probably just excited. I'm also not sure why I was BCC'd in the email, but maybe that's just how things work at NVIDIA. I'm extremely grateful for this opportunity, and am super glad that this is definitely real and not a scam.
